quotes.text: **iOS apps (US only)**: If you sell digital products, content, and subscriptions in the US, you can redirect customers to an external payment page using Stripe Checkout.
**Android apps (US only)**: You can process payments directly in-app with a third-party payment processor like Stripe.
[Use payment links (low-code)](https://docs.stripe.com/mobile/digital-goods/payment-links.md): Create a Payment Link for your in-app digital good or subscription.
[Use a custom in-app flow](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile.md): Use in-app payments to create a custom payment form directly in your Android app to accept in-app purchases.

findings: The 2026-11-07 capture and 2026-04-22 capture have the same platform statements, three accept-payment links, and customer-portal link. The 19-line diff only changes trailing whitespace on the Accept payments and Manage subscriptions headings; there is no substantive newly captured policy, API, eligibility, or integration behavior.

The page is a short navigation and overview route. Its US-only statements are scoped by platform and use 'can': an iOS app selling digital products, content, or subscriptions in the US can redirect to a Stripe Checkout external page (new line 11, old line 10); an Android US app can process directly in-app through a third-party processor such as Stripe (new line 13, old line 12). It links to separate implementation guides rather than proving app-store compliance or merchant eligibility itself.

The current source lines 13,19,34 and the Stripe index line 120 and in-app-payments concept lines 83,105 turn the overview's iOS 'can redirect' into a universal 'must redirect to Stripe Checkout' and call it the compliant target; the source also asserts no equivalent Android restriction. Those are pre-existing stronger claims, not changes established by either overview capture. They warrant separate review against actual platform rules and detailed Stripe guides, preserving jurisdiction, platform, app type, version, and eligibility conditions.

The source line 19 and related concept should not erase the distinct Payment Links route at new line 21/old line 20. The custom in-app form at new line 23/old line 22 is explicitly Android, while the customer portal at new line 27/old line 26 is a subscription-management redirect, not a payment acceptance method.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the old captured US-only iOS and Android scopes, the conditional 'can' wording, and the distinction between external Checkout redirect and direct Android in-app processing.

Preserve links to Checkout, Payment Links, Android custom in-app flow, and customer portal as separate navigation paths without promoting this index page to implementation or app-store-policy authority.
Retain the 2026-04-22 raw as the existing historical reference; the November navigation-only duplicate need not be added to factual raw_files solely for whitespace.
conflicts: Current source lines 13,19,34, Stripe index line 120, and wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md lines 83,105 overstate the index page's conditional US iOS Checkout route as an unconditional must or verified compliant target.
Current source line 34 says Android has no equivalent restriction, which neither dated overview capture establishes; both only say US Android apps can use a third-party in-app processor like Stripe.
Current source line 19's Checkout-only wording obscures the separate Payment Links navigation option at both new line 21 and old line 20.
unresolved_questions: This overview does not identify app-store rule versions, jurisdictions beyond its US labels, product or developer eligibility conditions, or whether a specific iOS or Android app is allowed to use these external or in-app payment paths.

Detailed implementation and platform-compliance assertions require the linked Checkout, Payment Links, in-app payments, and platform-policy sources; they cannot be concluded from this navigation-page recollection alone.
